The dataset **"subset_white_final_IB_dic.Rdata"** contains all processed variables needed for IB mediations (**AFTER** transformations and stress categories creation).

```{r}
load("../data/subset_white_final_IB_dic.Rdata")
stressor_categories_score_key=readRDS("../data/stressor_categories_score_key.RData")
library(dplyr)
```


# 2) AGE - Moderated Mediations:

```{r}
# List of IBs:
IBs = c("C4BCRP", "C4BMSDIL6", "C4BSESEL", "C4BSICAM", "C4BMSDTNFa")

# List all new stressors (categories) :
stressors_cat= stressor_categories_score_key$score_var

```


```{r}
##################### Create the output table to storage the mediation and moderation results:

### Function for marking p-values based on significance:
# @param pval - the pvalue
# @return - returns a significance marker similar to how R marks significance
mark_pvals <- function(pval){
  if (pval < 0.001){
    return("***")
  } else if (pval < 0.01){
    return("**")
  } else if (pval < 0.05){
    return("*")
  } else if(pval < 0.1){
    return(".")
  } else return(" ")
}

### Function for safely extracting stressor and IB names from result keys:
# This is needed because some stressor names contain underscores.
split_stress_ib_key <- function(result_key) {
  matched_IB <- IBs[sapply(IBs, function(x) endsWith(result_key, paste0("_", x)))]
  
  if (length(matched_IB) != 1) {
    stop("Could not identify a unique IB from result key: ", result_key)
  }
  
  IB <- matched_IB[1]
  stressor <- sub(paste0("_", IB, "$"), "", result_key)
  
  return(list(stressor = stressor, IB = IB))
}


### Function for making table of summary mediation and moderation results (into csv):
# @param - med.list: the list containing all the summary stats for the MEDIATION
# @param - mod.list: the list containing all the summary stats for the MODeration
# @param - moderator: the type of moderator, i.e., sex or age
# @param - CF: the cognitive function variable
# @param - sum.df: the pre-existing data frame I want to add the summary to
tabulate_results <- function(med.list, mod.list, moderator, CF, sum.df = NULL){
  # Create a list with column names for the table:
  c.n <- c("Moderator", "Stressor",	"IB",	"CF",	
           # 1) Mediations: Indirect effect-ACME results:
           "MED: Ind_effect_ACME (Estimate)",	"MED: Ind_effect_ACME (CI Lower)",	"MED: Ind_effect_ACME (CI Upper)",	
           "MED: Ind_effect_ACME (p-value)",	"MED: Ind_effect_ACME (pvalue-marking)", "MED: Proportion_mediated_ACME (avg)",
           # 2) Moderations: Indirect effect-ACME results:
           "Mod: Ind_effect_ACME (Estimate)",	"Mod: Ind_effect_ACME (CI Lower)",	"Mod: Ind_effect_ACME (CI Upper)",	
           "Mod: Ind_effect_ACME (p-value)",	"Mod: Ind_effect_ACME (pvalue-marking)", 
           # 3) Mediations: Direct effect-ADE results:
           "MED: Dir_effect_ADE (Estimate)",	"MED: Dir_effect_ADE (CI Lower)",	"MED: Dir_effect_ADE (CI Upper)",	
           "MED: Dir_effect_ADE (p-value)",	"MED: Dir_effect_ADE (pvalue-marking)",
           # 4) Moderations: Direct effect-ADE results:
           "Mod: Dir_effect_ADE (Estimate)", "Mod: Dir_effect_ADE (CI Lower)",	"Mod: Dir_effect_ADE (CI Upper)",	
           "Mod: Dir_effect_ADE (p-value)",	"Mod: Dir_effect_ADE (pvalue-marking)")
  
  # Initialize a new dataframe:
  if (is.null(sum.df)){
    sum.df <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 25, nrow = 0))
    colnames(sum.df) <- c.n # Assign column names
  }
  
  # Iterate through all mediation results stored in med.list:
  for (l in names(med.list)){
    # Extract stressor and IB names from the stored keys:
    stress_and_IB <- split_stress_ib_key(l)
    stressor <- stress_and_IB$stressor
    IB <- stress_and_IB$IB
    lSum.df <- summary(med.list[[l]]) # Extract summary results from MEDIATION analysis
    lMod.list <- mod.list[[l]] # Extract summary results from MOderation analysis
    
    # Populate the table row by row:
    new.r <- c(
      moderator, stressor, IB, CF, 
      # 1) Mediations: Indirect effect-ACME results:
      lSum.df$d.avg, lSum.df$d.avg.ci[1], lSum.df$d.avg.ci[2], 
      formatC(lSum.df$d.avg.p, format = "f", digits = 5), # p-value with 5 decimal points
      mark_pvals(lSum.df$d.avg.p), lSum.df$n.avg,
      # 2) Moderations: Indirect effect-ACME results:
      lMod.list[[1]]$statistic, lMod.list[[1]]$conf.int[1], lMod.list[[1]]$conf.int[2], 
      formatC(lMod.list[[1]]$p.value, format = "f", digits = 5), 
      mark_pvals(lMod.list[[1]]$p.value), 
      # 3) Mediations: Direct effect-ADE results:
      lSum.df$z.avg, lSum.df$z.avg.ci[1], lSum.df$z.avg.ci[2], 
      formatC(lSum.df$z.avg.p, format = "f", digits = 5), 
      mark_pvals(lSum.df$z.avg.p),
      # 4) Moderations: Direct effect-ADE results:
      lMod.list[[2]]$statistic, lMod.list[[2]]$conf.int[1], lMod.list[[2]]$conf.int[2], 
      formatC(lMod.list[[2]]$p.value, format = "f", digits = 5), 
      mark_pvals(lMod.list[[2]]$p.value)
    )
    
    # Append each row to the summary dataframe:
    nr <- nrow(sum.df)
    sum.df[nr+1,] <- new.r # Add each row below the last existent
  } 
  return(sum.df)
}
```



###*CF-Linear:

I am going to use robust standard errors in the mediations (Model Y = linear models) to mitigate the impact of outliers and slightly skewed residuals.  

```{r}
library(mediation)
library(sandwich) # Used to get Heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors (robust standard errors) (used to allow the fitting of a model that does contain heteroskedastic residuals)
```

```{r}
### Helper to run one AGE-moderated mediation with a fallback model:
# The full model is always tried first. If the full model has NA coefficients because of a singular design matrix, the outcome model is refit without the 3-way interaction stress:IB:age. If needed, the mediator model is also simplified by removing stress:age. This keeps the original modeling strategy whenever possible and only simplifies models that would otherwise fail.
run_age_mediation_pair <- function(outcome, outcome_family, stress, IB, data,
                                   sims = 1000, age_low = 45, age_high = 65) {
  covariates <- "C1PRSEX + SES + C1SBMI + C1SA26F + C1SA11T"
  
  formula_M_full <- as.formula(
    paste(IB, "~", stress, "* C1PRAGE +", covariates)
  )
  
  formula_Y_full <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, "~", stress, "*", IB, "* C1PRAGE +", covariates)
  )
  
  # Use the same complete-case data for both models and drop unused factor levels.
  model_vars <- unique(c(all.vars(formula_M_full), all.vars(formula_Y_full)))
  model_data <- droplevels(na.omit(data[, model_vars]))
  
  stress_values <- sort(unique(model_data[[stress]]))
  cat("Stress distribution for ", stress, ":\n", sep = "")
  print(table(model_data[[stress]], useNA = "ifany"))
  
  if (length(stress_values) < 2) {
    cat("Skipping ", stress, " and ", IB, ": stress has fewer than 2 observed values after complete-case filtering.\n", sep = "")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  control_stress_value <- min(stress_values)
  treat_stress_value <- max(stress_values)
  
  model_M <- lm(formula_M_full, data = model_data)
  model_Y <- glm(formula_Y_full, family = outcome_family, data = model_data)
  model_used <- "full_age_moderated_model"
  
  # First fallback: keep age moderation but remove the highest-order outcome interaction.
  if (anyNA(coef(model_M)) || anyNA(coef(model_Y))) {
    cat("Singular full model for ", stress, " and ", IB, "; retrying without stress:IB:C1PRAGE.\n", sep = "")
    
    formula_Y_no_3way <- as.formula(
      paste(outcome, "~", stress, "* C1PRAGE +", IB, "* C1PRAGE +", stress, "*", IB, "+", covariates)
    )
    
    model_Y <- glm(formula_Y_no_3way, family = outcome_family, data = model_data)
    model_used <- "fallback_no_3way_outcome_interaction"
  }
  
  # Second fallback: if the mediator model is singular, remove stress:age there too.
  if (anyNA(coef(model_M)) || anyNA(coef(model_Y))) {
    cat("Model still singular for ", stress, " and ", IB, "; retrying with simplified mediator model.\n", sep = "")
    
    formula_M_no_interaction <- as.formula(
      paste(IB, "~", stress, "+ C1PRAGE +", covariates)
    )
    
    formula_Y_no_3way <- as.formula(
      paste(outcome, "~", stress, "* C1PRAGE +", IB, "* C1PRAGE +", stress, "*", IB, "+", covariates)
    )
    
    model_M <- lm(formula_M_no_interaction, data = model_data)
    model_Y <- glm(formula_Y_no_3way, family = outcome_family, data = model_data)
    model_used <- "fallback_no_3way_and_simplified_mediator"
  }
  
  if (anyNA(coef(model_M)) || anyNA(coef(model_Y))) {
    cat("Skipping ", stress, " and ", IB, ": model still has NA coefficients.\n", sep = "")
    print(coef(model_M)[is.na(coef(model_M))])
    print(coef(model_Y)[is.na(coef(model_Y))])
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  mediations_a <- tryCatch(
    mediate(
      model_M,
      model_Y,
      treat = stress,
      mediator = IB,
      robustSE = TRUE,
      sims = sims,
      treat.value = treat_stress_value,
      control.value = control_stress_value
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("Skipping ", stress, " and ", IB, ": mediate() failed - ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = "")
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(mediations_a)) return(NULL)
  
  moderations_a <- tryCatch(
    test.modmed(
      mediations_a,
      list(C1PRAGE = age_low),
      list(C1PRAGE = age_high)
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("Skipping ", stress, " and ", IB, ": test.modmed() failed - ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = "")
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(moderations_a)) return(NULL)
  
  return(list(
    mediation = mediations_a,
    moderation = moderations_a,
    model_used = model_used,
    treat.value = treat_stress_value,
    control.value = control_stress_value
  ))
}
```



#### A) Executive Function (C3TCTFLU) - linear:

```{r}
# Initialize lists to store mediation and moderation results:
set.seed(1234)
mediation_results_a <- list()
moderation_results_a <- list()
mediation_model_used_a <- list()

# Loop through each IB:
for (IB in IBs) {
  # Loop through each stress variable
  for (stress in stressors_cat) {
    
    # Track running:
    cat("Running: ", stress, " and ", IB, "\n")
    
    ### 1-5) Fit models, run mediation, and run age moderation test:
    mediation_pair <- run_age_mediation_pair(
      outcome = "C3TCTFLU",
      outcome_family = gaussian(link = "identity"), # Quantitative outcome
      stress = stress,
      IB = IB,
      data = subset_white_final_IB_dic
    )
    
    if (is.null(mediation_pair)) next
    
    # Store results
    mediation_results_a[[paste(stress, IB, sep = "_")]] <- mediation_pair$mediation
    moderation_results_a[[paste(stress, IB, sep = "_")]] <- mediation_pair$moderation
    mediation_model_used_a[[paste(stress, IB, sep = "_")]] <- mediation_pair$model_used
  }
}

# Print all mediation results
for (result in names(mediation_results_a)) {
  stress_and_IB <- split_stress_ib_key(result)
  stress <- stress_and_IB$stressor
  IB <- stress_and_IB$IB
  cat("1) Executive Function (C3TCTFLU): Mediation result of the stressor:", stress, ", and the IB", IB, ":\n")
  print(summary(mediation_results_a[[result]]))
  
  # Print moderation results:
  cat("\n 2) Moderation Test (Age 40 vs 75):\n")
  print(moderation_results_a[[paste(stress, IB, sep = "_")]])
}


## Apply the function to create the output table:
IB_age.df <- tabulate_results(mediation_results_a, moderation_results_a, "Age", "Immediate Episodic Memory (C3TWLITU)")

```

###*CF-Poisson:

Although overdisperssion tests (Model_Y) using these CF variables indicated that the dispersion was ok, I will still use robust standard errors to mitigate the impact of some outliers in Model_M.
